title: Watch Target Detected Event
description: An inbound message on some channel was matched to a watched target (a person or organisation the operator keeps watch on). The fact is target-focused, not provider-focused: provider names the channel it arrived on (the entity segment of the source type), and any provider whose inbound schema carries an x-sender block (docs/event-naming.md, section 10) is matched without a change here. The event id is deterministic, uuid5(watch_id + ':' + dedupe_key), so a replayed source event or a near-duplicate delivery collapses to one detection; causationid is the source event's id. ordering_key is watch:<watch_id>: every fact about one target orders together. Handles the target matched on (matched_on) and the sender are personal data: a producer never publishes a detection for a target outside its own target files, and the repo never carries real handles.

ordering_key.description: Section 11.1 bucket 'watch:<watch_id>', the same value as 'watch:' + data.watch_id.

watch_id.description: The target's id from its watch file, lowercase slug (for example 'jane-doe'). Names the ordering bucket.

target_display_name.description: Human-readable name of the target for alerts and ticket titles.

provider.description: The channel the message arrived on: the entity segment of source_type (email, rcs, sms, telegram, slack, google_chat, call, ...). The matcher may refine a call event to 'voicemail' when the recording is a voicemail. Open-ended on purpose: a new provider appears here without a schema change.

source_type.description: Full CloudEvents type of the inbound event that was matched, for example bloodbank.messaging.rcs.received.

source_event_id.description: CloudEvents id of the inbound event; the envelope causationid carries the same value.

matched_on.description: Which of the target's handles matched the sender.

kind.description: Handle kind, the same vocabulary as x-sender.handle_kinds.

value.description: The normalised handle that matched (lowercased email, E.164, casefolded label, or platform:id).

sender.description: The sender as the source event named them, before normalisation.

handle.description: Sender handle exactly as it appeared in the source event.

display_name.description: Sender display name, when the source exposed one.

conversation.description: The conversation the message belongs to, for coalescing follow-ups.

thread_id.description: Provider-native thread, chat or call id; null when the source names none.

group_label.description: Group chat title when the message came through a group ('<group>: <name>' sender labels); null for a one-to-one message.

text.description: Message text, truncated to 4000 characters. Empty for a call or recording with no transcript.

subject.description: Subject line, when the provider has one (email).

received_at.description: When the provider received the message (source clock), RFC 3339.

dedupe_key.description: Stable key of this (target, message) pair: the event id is uuid5(watch_id + ':' + dedupe_key). Normally the source event's message or call id.
